result.title: Reason or Recite: Complementary Specialists with an LLM Judge for Traffic Anomaly Reasoning
result.comment: 18 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the AI City Challenge Workshop, ECCV 2026. 1st place in Track 3 (Traffic Anomaly Reasoning)
result.summary: Road anomalies such as collisions, violations, and sudden hazards demand more from video understanding than detection: a practical system must verify what happened, describe the scene, and explain the cause. We find these competences pull in opposite directions for vision-language models: closed-form questions reward precise, evidence-grounded reasoning, while open-ended answers are scored by similarity to reference text, where matching the annotation style matters as much as reasoning correctly. We present Reason-or-Recite (RoR), a two-specialist framework for the Traffic Anomaly Reasoning track of the 2026 AI City Challenge. RoR (1) rewrites the official chain-of-thought annotations into a structured, temporally grounded schema and LoRA-tunes a 9B vision-language model on the enhanced traces; (2) fine-tunes a 4-bit-quantized 27B model on answers alone, absorbing the annotation style; and (3) selects between the two candidates per question with a training-free LLM judge. RoR ranks first on the in-domain leaderboard with mean score 0.6788.

AI.brief_summary: 面向交通异常视频问答，将官方CoT标注改写为结构化、带时间定位的schema并对9B VLM做LoRA微调，另用4-bit量化的27B模型只学答案风格，最后由免训练LLM裁判逐题择优。
